ownerIdentityResolution.location: projectos/agent/src/planApproval.ts:1142, calling resolveRecordedOwner(sys, root, config, proposal.projectId, 'committed')
ownerIdentityResolution.finding: Called with planTrust='committed'. Inside resolveRecordedOwner (line 920-1054): when an active plan is declared, the working-tree declaration is cross-checked against the COMMITTED declaration and refused on mismatch (NO_ACTIVE_PLAN); the actual plan bytes used to extract governance.owner are then read via readCommittedJson, never from the working tree. When no plan is declared (genesis/first-plan case), eligibility itself is checked against the COMMITTED project-config, and the owner is read from the COMMITTED genesis record only. The function's own comment at line 962 self-labels this block '// C11-W2-F5. WHICH PLAN IS THE TRUST ANCHOR IS ITSELF A TRUSTED FACT.'

projectIdResolution.finding: trustedProjectId is read via readCommittedJson(sys, root, PROJECT_CONFIG_REL) — committed bytes only. Compared against proposal.projectId (the working-tree candidate); any established project (one with a committed project-config.json) that disagrees is refused with PROJECT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH before resolveRecordedOwner is even called.

planMemoryPlanPathResolution.finding: The working-tree declared path is read only to select a branch; under planTrust='committed' it is cross-validated against the COMMITTED project-config's own planMemory.planPath declaration, and any disagreement is refused (NO_ACTIVE_PLAN) before the path is used to read plan content — and that content read is itself from the committed tree (readCommittedJson), never the working copy.
